checks.text: The page displays the heading "Gradebook Manager" and a grid whose column headers are "Student", "Math", "Science", "English" and "Average", with one empty row.
In the first row, typing "Alice" in the Student input, "95" in Math, "88" in Science and "92" in English displays "91.67" in the Average cell of that row immediately (no Tab needed).

After the Alice row of A2, clicking the button "Add Student" adds a second row; typing "Bob" in its Student input, "70" in Math, "75" in Science and "80" in English displays "75.00" in the Average cell of Bob's row.

From the empty page, clicking the button "Add Student" adds a new empty row below the existing empty row: the grid then has two data rows, each with empty Student, Math, Science and English inputs and an empty Average cell.

With Alice (95, 88, 92) in row 1 and Bob (70, 75, 80) in row 2, clicking the button "Select Alice" in Alice's row header and then the button "Delete Student" removes Alice's row: the grid has one data row, Bob's, whose Average cell shows "75.00".

With Alice (95, 88, 92) and Bob (70, 75, 80) entered, clicking the tab "Statistics" shows "Class Average: 83.33", "Highest: 95", "Lowest: 70" and "Median: 84.00". (All six scores: sum 500, mean 500/6 = 83.33; sorted 70, 75, 80, 88, 92, 95, median (80+88)/2 = 84.00.)

With only Bob (70, 75, 80) entered, in the Statistics tab clicking the button "Export CSV" copies this text to the clipboard: "Student,Math,Science,English,Average\nBob,70,75,80,75.00" (CSV rows never include empty trailing rows).
With only Bob entered (70, 75, 80), changing Bob's Math value to "105" displays "86.67" in Bob's Average cell ((105+75+80)/3 = 260/3 = 86.67), and the Statistics tab shows "Highest: 105".
With only Bob entered (70, 75, 80), reloading the page keeps the data: Bob's row has Student "Bob", Math 70, Science 75, English 80 and Average "75.00".
